t: You're looking at Frobisher Crescent, a mid-rise terrace block on the Barbican Estate. It takes its name from Martin Frobisher, the Elizabethan sea captain and privateer. He made three voyages to the New World, searching for the North-west Passage. He probably sighted Resolution Island near Labrador, then entered Frobisher Bay and landed on what is now Baffin Island. So here, among the concrete terraces of the Barbican, a name quietly recalls an age of Arctic exploration.
